question.text: An investment proposal coming to the IC of 'Lotus Growth' Cat II AIF should typically contain which of the following information as per chapter best practice?

answer.text: Executive Summary, Company Overview, Market and Industry Overview, Financial Overview, Risks and Key DD areas, Valuation Overview, Exit strategy, Deal Structure/Term Sheet, and Recommendations
Only the proposed investment amount and valuation
Only the founder's personal references and educational background
A single-page summary restricted to pricing and expected IRR

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.7.3, an IC investment proposal should cover: Executive Summary, Company Overview (history, products, customers, suppliers, competitors, team bios), Market/Industry Overview, Financial Overview (historical and projected), Risks and Key DD Areas, Valuation Overview, Exit strategy, Deal Structure and Term Sheet Conditions, and Recommendations with Proposed Size and Structure. The Trap: Options A and D understate the required content. Option C is irrelevant to IC decision-making. Cross-Exam Context: IC-memo content tested in XIX-C and in XV (Research Analyst) for investment-memo discipline. Manager's Pro-Tip: Standardize the IC-memo template across all deals. Consistency lets IC members benchmark across deals and forces the investment team to fill uncomfortable gaps (e.g., exit strategy for illiquid investees).
